passages.title: 합병 후 중복 조직 통합 원칙 메일
passages.passage:
From: Integration Management Office
To: Divisional Leadership, Both Legacy Organizations
Subject: Overlapping Functions — Selection Principles, Stated Before Names

Dear Colleagues,

Within six weeks, we will announce the combined organization for the eleven functions where both legacy companies field full teams. Before any name is decided, the principles deserve publication — because a process trusted only after the results suit you is not trust.

Principle one: roles are designed before candidates are considered. Each combined function's mandate, size, and success measures are being written by the integration office with external facilitation — not by either incumbent leader, for reasons that need no elaboration.

Principle two: selection is evidence-based and two-sided. Every candidate for a contested role presents their function's last three years — decisions, outcomes, and, deliberately, the calls they got wrong and corrected — to a panel drawn from both legacy boards plus one external assessor. The 'wrong and corrected' element is not decoration: how leaders metabolize error predicts integration behavior better than any success narrative.

Principle three: the runner-up conversation happens with the same care as the appointment. Strong leaders who lose contested roles receive concrete alternatives — expanded adjacent mandates, integration leadership positions, or, where preferences run that way, supported exits with full vesting. A merger that hemorrhages the acquired company's talent has purchased an org chart, not a business.

Timeline, panel composition, and appeal mechanics follow next week. Until announcements, both legacy structures hold full authority — a vacuum of six weeks is survivable; a vacuum of authority is not.

Integration Management Office

questions.q: Why are roles designed before candidates?
choices: To prevent incumbents shaping roles around themselves
questions.exKo: 현직 리더가 자신에게 맞춰 직무를 설계하는 것을 막기 위해서입니다.

questions.q: Why must candidates present corrected mistakes?
choices: Error handling predicts integration behavior better than successes
questions.exKo: 실수를 소화하는 방식이 성공담보다 통합 이후 행동을 잘 예측하기 때문입니다.

questions.q: What does the runner-up principle aim to prevent?
choices: Talent loss that leaves an org chart without a business
questions.exKo: 탈락한 인재의 유출로 조직도만 남는 인수를 막으려는 것입니다.

passages.title: 연구 성과 상업화 갈등 조정 메일
passages.passage:
From: Chief Technology Officer
To: VP Research, VP Product
Subject: The Catalyst Dispute — A Decision Framework, Not a Verdict

Ana, Tomas,

Your escalations crossed in my inbox, which tells me the catalyst project needs an arbiter less than it needs a framework — verdicts settle arguments; frameworks prevent their sequels.

The dispute, restated fairly: Research wants six more months to publish the mechanism and file broader patents; Product wants immediate commercialization from the current, narrower understanding, citing two competitors circling the same chemistry. Both positions are correct within their mandates, which is why neither can yield gracefully.

The framework I am imposing: we file the narrow patents now — this week — because filing dates are the one resource that cannot be recovered. Simultaneously, the publication moves forward with a 90-day commercial review gate, not the six months Research requested nor the zero Product implied: competitors reverse-engineer shipped products within a quarter anyway, so secrecy beyond one quarter defends little while costing us the academic priority that recruits our next generation of chemists.

Revenue mechanics: the pilot line proceeds against the narrow claims, with the broader patents joining the estate as they mature. If the mechanism publication triggers competitor filings, our priority date already stands — that is what this week's filing buys.

Neither of you gets your full position; both of you get the part your mandate actually requires. Object by Thursday with evidence, not preference — after that, we execute.

Elena

questions.q: Why does the CTO file narrow patents immediately?
questions.exKo: 출원일은 나중에 되찾을 수 없는 유일한 자원이기 때문입니다.

questions.q: Why is long secrecy judged low-value?
choices: Shipped products are reverse-engineered within a quarter anyway
questions.exKo: 출시 제품은 한 분기면 역설계되므로 그 이상의 비밀 유지는 실익이 적습니다.

questions.q: What does the closing line demand of objections?
questions.exKo: 목요일까지 선호가 아닌 근거를 갖춰 이의를 제기하라고 요구합니다.

passages.title: 야간 교대 건강 보호 프로그램 공지
passages.passage:
NIGHT SHIFT HEALTH PROGRAM — WHAT CHANGES AND WHY

The medical literature on rotating night work has grown too consistent to file under 'general wellness': circadian disruption elevates measurable risks that our own occupational health data mirrors. Rather than restate studies, this notice states responses.

Scheduling: rotation direction becomes uniformly forward — mornings to evenings to nights — which the sleep research shows bodies tolerate measurably better than backward rotation; consecutive night blocks cap at four, followed by a minimum 48-hour reset. The scheduling system enforces both automatically, and exceptions require occupational health sign-off, not merely supervisor convenience.

Environment: night-shift areas receive circadian lighting this quarter — higher intensity early shift, warmer and dimmer toward morning — and the canteen's night service moves from reheated day surplus to a menu designed for nocturnal metabolism, a change the pilot site's shift councils rated their highest-impact item, above every scheduling adjustment.

Health monitoring: annual screenings for night workers expand to include the cardiovascular and metabolic markers the literature flags, with results confidential to the individual and occupational health — aggregated trends inform the program; individual data never reaches management.

Compensation: night differentials rise 15 percent — but the program's premise deserves stating plainly: money does not metabolize risk. The differential compensates inconvenience; the redesign above addresses the health substance, and conflating the two is how industries buy silence instead of safety.

Shift council consultations begin Tuesday.

Occupational Health & Operations

questions.q: Why does rotation become uniformly forward?
choices: Bodies tolerate forward rotation measurably better
questions.exKo: 수면 연구상 정방향 순환(아침→저녁→밤)이 신체 부담이 적기 때문입니다.

questions.q: What did pilot shift councils rate highest?
questions.exKo: 야간 대사에 맞춘 식단 개선을 일정 조정보다 높게 평가했습니다.

questions.q: What point does the compensation paragraph make?
choices: Money compensates inconvenience but cannot replace health redesign
questions.exKo: 수당은 불편의 보상일 뿐, 돈으로 위험을 대사시킬 수는 없다는 원칙입니다.

passages.title: 입찰 참여 윤리 기준 강화 공지
passages.passage:
BID CONDUCT STANDARDS — REINFORCED AFTER NEAR MISS

Last month, a competitor's confidential pricing document reached a member of our bid team through a former colleague — unsolicited, unopened beyond the subject line, and reported within an hour. That report triggered this notice, because the near miss deserves to become doctrine while it is fresh.

What the team did right is now the mandatory protocol: do not open, do not forward, do not summarize from memory to teammates. Report to legal immediately; legal quarantines the material, documents the chain, and — as in this case — notifies the tender authority proactively. The authority's response is instructive: our disclosure preserved our eligibility, while an undisclosed receipt discovered later would have disqualified the bid and likely triggered a debarment review reaching every public tender we hold.

The wider rules, restated: we do not seek competitors' bid information through any channel, including 'market intelligence' consultants whose methods we cannot audit — engaging such consultants now requires legal's pre-approval of their sourcing methodology in writing. Former employees of competitors joining our teams observe a 12-month recusal from bids against their previous employer — protecting them as much as us, since they are the first suspects when information surfaces.

Pricing folders move to need-to-know access with watermarked copies, not from distrust of colleagues but because our own document reaching a competitor would test their ethics with our commercial future — a test no one should be handed the chance to fail.

Ethics & Legal

questions.q: What did the team member do correctly?
choices: Reported the unopened document within an hour
questions.exKo: 제목 외에는 열지 않고 한 시간 내에 법무팀에 신고했습니다.

questions.q: What did proactive disclosure preserve?
questions.exKo: 선제 공개가 입찰 자격을 지켰고, 은폐 후 발각 시 전면 배제될 뻔했습니다.

questions.q: Why the 12-month recusal for competitor hires?
choices: It protects them as first suspects when leaks surface
questions.exKo: 정보 유출 시 첫 의심 대상이 되는 본인을 보호하는 장치이기도 합니다.

passages.title: 협동로봇 도입 컨설팅 광고
passages.passage:
COBOTIC WORKS — AUTOMATION THAT YOUR BEST PEOPLE DESIGN

The automation graveyard is full of robots specified by consultants who visited for a week and left before the exceptions started. The workaround your veteran operator performs at 2 P.M. every Thursday — undocumented, load-bearing, invisible in the process map — is precisely what breaks the textbook deployment.

Cobotic Works inverts the method. Our engineers embed with your shift teams for the diagnostic month, and the operators who know the exceptions co-design the automation — deciding what the robot takes and, as critically, what stays human. Deployments designed this way survive contact with reality: our 140 installations run at 92 percent sustained utilization against an industry norm near 60, the difference being not better robots but better-placed ones.

The workforce mechanics are contractual, not aspirational: every deployment includes funded operator training to robot supervision and programming roles, and we decline engagements framed as headcount elimination — not from sentiment, but track record: plants that automate against their workforce sabotage the payback quietly and unprovably, while plants that automate with them staff our reference list.

Start with the two-week feasibility sprint: your operators, our engineers, one production cell, and a business case in numbers your CFO will audit rather than admire. cobotic.works/sprint.

questions.q: What breaks textbook automation, per the ad?
choices: Undocumented workarounds invisible in process maps
questions.exKo: 공정도에 없는 베테랑 작업자의 비공식 예외 처리가 배치를 무너뜨립니다.

questions.q: What explains the 92 percent utilization?
choices: Operators co-designing what automates and what stays human
questions.exKo: 더 좋은 로봇이 아니라 현장이 함께 설계한 '더 잘 배치된' 로봇 덕분입니다.

questions.q: Why does the firm decline headcount-elimination framings?
choices: Workforces automated against quietly sabotage the payback
questions.exKo: 직원을 겨냥한 자동화는 보이지 않는 방식으로 투자 회수를 망가뜨리기 때문입니다.

passages.title: 수출 통제 스크리닝 자동화 광고
passages.passage:
CLEARGATE — EXPORT COMPLIANCE AT TRANSACTION SPEED

Your sales team closes in minutes; your export screening runs on Thursdays. Between those two clocks lives every violation your company will ever commit — shipped in good faith, discovered in an audit, punished as if intended.

ClearGate screens every order, quote, and shipment in real time against restricted-party lists, dual-use classifications, and destination controls across 40 regulatory regimes — updated continuously, because sanctioned entities change names faster than quarterly training can mention them. Ambiguous matches route to your compliance officer with the evidence assembled: corporate family trees, alias histories, and the specific list logic that fired, cutting resolution from hours of searching to minutes of judgment.

The design principle is friction-proportionality: clean transactions — the overwhelming majority — clear invisibly in milliseconds, while genuine risk gets undivided attention. Blanket slowdowns teach sales teams to route around compliance; invisible clearance makes the compliant path the fast path, which is the only compliance architecture that survives quota pressure.

Audit mode reconstructs any decision with its full evidence state as of that moment — regulators receive answers, not apologies. Integration with major ERPs ships standard; classification assistance for your product catalog is included in onboarding. Priced by transaction volume: cleargate.trade.

questions.q: Where do violations live, per the ad's framing?
choices: In the gap between sales speed and screening speed
questions.exKo: 분 단위 영업과 주 단위 심사 사이의 시차에서 위반이 발생합니다.

questions.q: Why must screening lists update continuously?
choices: Sanctioned entities change names faster than training cycles
questions.exKo: 제재 대상이 분기 교육보다 빨리 이름을 바꾸기 때문입니다.

questions.q: Why is friction-proportionality essential?
choices: Blanket slowdowns push sales to bypass compliance entirely
questions.exKo: 일괄 지연은 영업이 컴플라이언스를 우회하게 만들므로, 준법 경로가 가장 빨라야 합니다.

passages.title: 대체 단백질 산업 구조조정 기사
passages.passage:
FOOD INDUSTRY — The alternative-protein sector's capital winter has produced its first structural survivors, and their common traits sketch the industry's probable shape more accurately than the boom-year projections ever did.

The washout was severe: sector funding fell 70 percent from peak, three high-profile startups liquidated, and retail sales of first-generation products declined for eight consecutive quarters as repeat purchase rates — the metric the category hid longest — settled near 30 percent against the 60-plus of successful food launches. The autopsy consensus: products marketed as replacements invited a comparison they lost on taste and price simultaneously, a two-front war no food category has ever won.

The survivors share three departures from that playbook. They sell as ingredients to food manufacturers rather than as branded replacements — disappearing into products consumers already accept. They compete on function — heat stability, protein density, cost-per-nutrition — where their technology holds genuine advantages, rather than on mimicry, where it does not yet. And they manufacture through partnerships with existing food-processing capacity rather than building the gleaming dedicated plants that consumed the liquidated companies' capital: asset-light survived; asset-heavy did not.

Analysts note the pattern echoes earlier ingredient revolutions — soy lecithin and whey protein entered the food system invisibly decades before any consumer brand claimed them. 'The category mistook a supply-chain innovation for a consumer movement,' one food-systems researcher concludes. 'The survivors corrected the diagnosis.'

questions.q: What metric did the category conceal longest?
questions.exKo: 성공 식품의 절반 수준인 30% 재구매율이 가장 오래 숨겨진 지표였습니다.

questions.q: How do survivors sell their products?
choices: As ingredients to manufacturers rather than branded replacements
questions.exKo: 대체품 브랜드가 아니라 식품 제조사용 원료로 공급합니다.

questions.q: What diagnosis error does the researcher identify?
choices: Mistaking a supply-chain innovation for a consumer movement
questions.exKo: 공급망 혁신을 소비자 운동으로 오인한 것이 범주 전체의 착오였습니다.

passages.title: 무역 결제 통화 다변화 기사
passages.passage:
TRADE FINANCE — Invoice currency, long the sleepiest field on a trade document, has become an active negotiation, and corporate treasurers are discovering that the choice embeds consequences reaching well beyond conversion fees.

Surveys of trade-finance banks report bilateral-currency invoicing — transactions priced in neither party's traditional vehicle currency — growing from the low single digits to 12 percent of documented flows in three years, concentrated in commodities, machinery, and intra-regional Asian trade. The drivers are practical rather than ideological: sanctions exposure has made some counterparties' banks cautious about dollar clearing's jurisdictional reach; hedging costs for certain currency pairs have fallen as offshore liquidity pools deepen; and large importers increasingly demand local-currency pricing as a term of volume commitments, shifting exchange risk upstream to sellers with thinner treasury capabilities.

That shift is the story beneath the story. Exporters accepting exotic-currency invoices without matching hedging capacity are accumulating risk they historically never held, and two mid-sized machinery firms' earnings restatements this year traced precisely to unhedged bilateral receivables. Banks have responded with bundled offerings — invoicing, hedging, and settlement in one facility — priced attractively enough to suggest they view the capability gap as a durable revenue stream.

Treasury consultants' advice has hardened into a rule: the invoice currency decision belongs to the CFO's office, not the sales team closing the deal — 'volume commitments look different when the exchange risk they carry is priced against them.'

questions.q: What is driving bilateral-currency invoicing?
choices: Practical factors like clearing caution and importer demands
questions.exKo: 달러 결제망 리스크, 헤지 비용 하락, 수입사의 자국 통화 요구 등 실무적 요인입니다.

questions.q: What is 'the story beneath the story'?
choices: Exchange risk shifting to sellers unequipped to hedge it
questions.exKo: 환리스크가 헤지 역량 없는 수출업체로 전가되고 있다는 점입니다.

questions.q: What rule have consultants adopted?
choices: Invoice currency decisions belong to the CFO, not sales
questions.exKo: 청구 통화 결정권은 딜을 성사시키려는 영업이 아니라 재무 부서에 있어야 한다는 원칙입니다.

passages.title: 임원 채용 배경조회 이상 신호 문자
passages.passage:
Sara Novak (5:40 P.M.)
Background check on our COO finalist came back. One flag: his 'VP Operations' title at Dexler was actually 'Senior Director' — the VP promotion he lists came two months after he'd already resigned.

Michael Chen (5:46 P.M.)
Hm. Material or cosmetic? People round up titles constantly, and Dexler's org was famously flat.

Sara Novak (5:48 P.M.)
That's the generous read. The stricter one: every other candidate survived the same verification cleanly, and this is a role whose first-year job includes certifying compliance filings. Precision about one's own record isn't decoration for that seat.

Michael Chen (5:51 P.M.)
Agreed it can't be ignored. Options: drop him quietly, or confront the discrepancy directly and calibrate on his response?

Sara Novak (5:53 P.M.)
Confront — but carefully. Tomorrow's final conversation, I show him the verification line and ask him to walk me through it. No ambush framing, one open question. What he does with it tells us more than the discrepancy itself.

Michael Chen (5:55 P.M.)
Scenarios?

Sara Novak (5:57 P.M.)
If he says 'the promotion was agreed before I left and I should have dated it precisely — that's on me,' that's a correctable honesty. If he argues the titles were 'functionally equivalent' or blames the HR system, that's how he'll handle a compliance discrepancy too — and we'll have learned it for the price of one awkward meeting.

Michael Chen (5:58 P.M.)
And the board packet?

Sara Novak (5:59 P.M.)
Either way, the packet includes the verification finding and his verbatim response. If we proceed, we proceed with open eyes — a hire this senior shouldn't rest on our editing.

Michael Chen (6:00 P.M.)
Agreed on all counts. Tell me how tomorrow goes.

questions.q: What did the background check reveal?
choices: A listed VP title that postdated his resignation
questions.exKo: 이력서의 VP 직함이 실제로는 퇴사 두 달 후에 부여된 것이었습니다.

questions.q: Why does the discrepancy matter for this role?
choices: The COO certifies compliance filings requiring personal precision
questions.exKo: 컴플라이언스 서류를 인증할 자리에는 자기 기록의 정확성이 필수입니다.

questions.q: What will the confrontation actually test?
choices: How he handles being confronted with a discrepancy
questions.exKo: 불일치 자체보다 그것을 다루는 태도가 향후 행동의 예고편이기 때문입니다.

passages.title: 생산 자동화 투자 시점 논쟁 문자
passages.passage:
Tom Eriksen (2:20 P.M.)
Board pre-read went out. Finance attached a dissent to our packaging automation proposal — 'wait 18 months, equipment prices are falling 8 percent annually.'

Priya Sharma (2:26 P.M.)
The dissent does honest math on the wrong equation. Equipment is 40 percent of project cost; falling prices save us maybe 3 percent of total. Meanwhile the line's overtime premium runs 30K monthly and rises with every wage round — waiting 18 months costs 540K to save roughly 200.

Tom Eriksen (2:28 P.M.)
Finance will counter that overtime is variable — demand could soften.

Priya Sharma (2:31 P.M.)
Could, but our order book says otherwise: 14 months of contracted volume, and the customer forecasts beyond that are the strongest in three years. And there's a cost the dissent doesn't model at all: we've had two near-miss injuries on the manual palletizing station this year. The insurer's engineer flagged it in writing. If one converts to an actual injury while a funded automation proposal sits deferred for price timing, the liability posture is indefensible — morally before legally.

Tom Eriksen (2:33 P.M.)
That argument belongs in the packet, stated exactly that plainly.

Priya Sharma (2:35 P.M.)
It will be. I'm also conceding their strongest point: we'll structure the vendor contract with price-adjustment sharing — if equipment indexes fall before delivery, we capture half the decline. Their insight gets captured; the delay gets rejected.

Tom Eriksen (2:36 P.M.)
Which turns the dissent into a contract clause instead of a postponement. They can vote for that with their argument honored.

Priya Sharma (2:37 P.M.)
Exactly. Revised packet to the board secretary by tomorrow noon.

questions.q: What is wrong with the dissent's math?
choices: Waiting costs far more in overtime than equipment savings
questions.exKo: 18개월 대기 시 초과근무 54만이 장비 절감 약 20만을 압도합니다.

questions.q: What unmodeled cost does Ms. Sharma raise?
choices: Injury liability from documented near misses on the manual station
questions.exKo: 보험사가 서면 경고한 수작업 구간의 부상 위험이 대기 비용에 빠져 있습니다.

questions.q: How is the dissent's insight preserved?
choices: A price-adjustment clause captures half of any equipment price decline
questions.exKo: 가격 하락분의 절반을 반영하는 계약 조항으로 지연 없이 반론을 수용합니다.
